problem_statement: IPv4 route handling has several gaps that surface in multi-interface / VPN setups. An explicit IPv4 default route (0.0.0.0/0) cannot be added: the route add path rejects any route whose destination is the unspecified address, even when the prefix length is 0, so a default route entry cannot be created, looked up, or returned via route-info. Locally originated IPv4 traffic (source/interface selection) does not consult the configured IPv4 route table: when the destination is not on the same subnet as the default interface, selection falls back to the default interface and ignores more specific host/prefix routes on other interfaces, so the wrong egress interface and source address are chosen. Routing a packet whose network interface has not been set is not rejected: the route-packet path only checks the nexthop and proceeds with a NULL interface instead of returning an error.
twister_command: scripts/twister -p native_sim/native/64 -T tests/net/route/ipv4 -s tests/net/route/ipv4/net.route.ipv4 -s net.route.ipv4 -O twister-out --no-clean -W

verification.reason: The statement only covers IPv4 behavior and never mentions the new Kconfig option names (CONFIG_NET_IPV4_FORWARDING, CONFIG_NET_IPV6_FORWARDING, CONFIG_NET_IPV4_ROUTE, CONFIG_NET_IPV6_ROUTE) that the test configurations require, nor the IPv6 behaviors the tests exercise. All gaps are repairable by expanding the statement to cover both address families, the Kconfig rename, and the missing-neighbor forwarding behavior.

problems.detail: The tests' prj.conf files use CONFIG_NET_IPV4_FORWARDING, CONFIG_NET_IPV4_ROUTE, and CONFIG_NET_IPV6_ROUTE, but the statement never mentions these Kconfig option names. The agent must create/rename these Kconfig symbols or the build will fail with unknown CONFIG options.

The statement describes only IPv4 gaps (default route, source/interface selection, NULL iface rejection), but the hidden tests also check IPv6 source/interface selection via route table (test_route_ipv6_select_src_iface_uses_explicit_route) and IPv6 NULL-iface rejection (test_route_ipv6_packet_without_iface). The statement must cover both families.

The test test_route_ipv6_packet_without_neighbor_ll checks that net_route_ipv6_packet succeeds (returns 0 and the packet is sent) when the destination neighbor is not found but the egress interface does not support link-layer addressing (e.g. a VPN/virtual interface). The statement does not describe this required behavior.

leak_check.leak_detail: The phrases describing that the route-add path rejects the unspecified address and that the route-packet path only checks the nexthop are implementation-leaning bug-cause descriptions. They are not essential to the required behavior and can be reworded without losing the requirements checked by the tests.
leak_check.suggested_statement: IPv4 and IPv6 route handling has several gaps that surface in multi-interface / VPN setups. An explicit IPv4 default route (0.0.0.0/0) cannot be created, looked up, or returned via route-info. Locally originated IPv4 and IPv6 traffic (source/interface selection) must consult the configured route table so that more specific host/prefix routes on other interfaces are used instead of falling back to the default interface, ensuring the correct egress interface and source address are chosen. Routing a packet whose network interface has not been set must be rejected with -EINVAL for both IPv4 and IPv6. For IPv6, routing a packet whose destination neighbor is not found must not fail when the egress interface does not support link-layer addressing (as with VPN or virtual interfaces); the packet should still be forwarded in that case. The per-family unicast route table options CONFIG_NET_IPV4_ROUTE and CONFIG_NET_IPV6_ROUTE enable static route management, shell route commands, and host-side route selection for locally originated traffic. The forwarding options CONFIG_NET_IPV4_FORWARDING and CONFIG_NET_IPV6_FORWARDING (renamed from the deprecated CONFIG_NET_IPV4_ROUTING and CONFIG_NET_IPV6_ROUTING) enable IP forwarding between interfaces and depend on the corresponding route table options.
